item.title: Vance blames Iran war for Republican losses in midterm elections
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows the U.S. Capitol building in Washington, D.C., the United States. (Xinhua/Li Rui)
WASHINGTON, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that the war against Iran was the reason Republicans lost in the midterm elections.
"The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," he wrote in a post on X.
His remarks came hours after U.S. President Donald Trump told The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) on Tuesday night that the war in Iran was partially to blame for widespread Republican losses in the midterm elections. Trump, however, said that he did not regret launching the war earlier this year.
"Iran was a piece of it," he said in a phone interview with the WSJ when asked whether the war contributed to Republicans' poor performance in the election.
He added that rising oil prices, rather than the war itself, were the biggest political liability.
In his latest post, Vance cited a pollster who had accurately predicted the election results, saying many voters who supported Trump in 2024 were angry and planned to vote for Democrats. The pollster asked former Republican voters what would bring them back to the party.
The top four responses were ending the war, focusing on the cost of living and inflation, putting the United States first, and changing Washington's relationship with Israel.
Democrats are projected to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, election forecasting agency Decision Desk HQ reported late Tuesday. Several media outlets described the outcome as a "blue wave" or even a "blue tsunami."
According to NBC News' latest projections, Democrats are expected to win at least 54 Senate seats, a net gain of seven from their pre-election total. They flipped several key battleground states, including Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine.
NBC News also projected that Democrats would win at least 238 House seats, a gain of 32, with the total expected to rise as vote counting continues.

item.title: China's top diplomat calls for new "golden decade" of Lancang-Mekong cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, co-chairs the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers' Meeting with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 4, 2026. Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn, Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Thongsavanh Phomvihane, Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung and Myanmar's Minister for the Ministry of National Planning, Investment and Foreign Economic Relations, Aung Kyaw Hoe, attended the meeting here on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)
BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday called on the six Lancang-Mekong countries to build on their fruitful cooperation in the past 10 years and jointly usher in a new "golden decade."
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when co-chairing with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Beijing.
The LMC mechanism was launched by the six countries in 2016. Its name derives from a river known as the Lancang in China and the Mekong after it flows out of the country and through Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.
China stands ready to work with Mekong countries in the direction set by the leaders, take stronger measures and more coordinated steps, to continuously substantiate the Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future, Wang said.
Wang called for efforts to keep Lancang-Mekong Cooperation at the forefront of regional cooperation, make it a benchmark for Global South solidarity, and contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity.
Lancang-Mekong countries should strengthen top-level design on core issues such as regional development and security, enhance the alignment of development strategies, promote trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, and deliver more "small and beautiful" livelihood demonstration projects to give people a greater sense of gain, he said.
It is important to expand cooperation in emerging fields such as the digital economy, artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing and smart agriculture, he said, welcoming more Mekong countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO).
He urged Lancang-Mekong countries to oppose external interference and incitement of bloc confrontation, reject the creation of exclusive "small circles," and never allow the resurgence of militarism, adding that the countries should step up joint efforts to combat cross-border crimes.
Wang suggested the countries promote the establishment of a Lancang-Mekong cross-border disaster early-warning cooperation mechanism and jointly enhance disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capabilities.
Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn, Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Thongsavanh Phomvihane, Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung and Myanmar's Minister for the Ministry of National Planning, Investment and Foreign Economic Relations, Aung Kyaw Hoe, attended the meeting.
All parties at the meeting spoke highly of the positive progress of the LMC over the past decade and appreciated China's important leading role in advancing their cooperation.
Those present reaffirmed their commitment to good-neighborliness and friendship, mutual respect and mutual trust, deeper cooperation and win-win outcomes, and to jointly promoting sustainable development and prosperity in the region.
They agreed to deepen cooperation in priority areas such as connectivity, water resources and environment, expand digital transformation, green innovation, and promote people-to-people and cultural exchanges.
They also agreed to strengthen disaster governance, tighten security coordination, combat cross-border crimes and safeguard regional tranquility.
All parties agreed to maintain close communication to ensure that the fifth LMC Leaders' Meeting is a complete success and delivers positive outcomes.

item.title: Chinese premier meets director general of WIPO
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Chinese Premier Li Qiang (R) meets with World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Director General Daren Tang in Beijing, China, on November 4, 2026. /Xinhua
Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Director General Daren Tang in Beijing on Wednesday.
China and WIPO have carried out fruitful cooperation in global intellectual property services, information technology, human resources and other fields in recent years, Li said.
China stands ready to work with WIPO to continuously deepen and solidify cooperation, promote international cooperation on intellectual property rights, and make greater contributions to global innovative development and common prosperity, Li added.
Li said China will continue to support WIPO's work and is willing to play a greater role in global intellectual property governance. It is hoped that WIPO will continue to support the development of China's intellectual property cause, build more platforms for exchanges and cooperation, and provide more convenient and high-quality services for Chinese users.
Congratulating China on the remarkable achievements made in its intellectual property cause, Tang noted that China has ranked among the top 10 in the Global Innovation Index with the largest number of top 100 innovation clusters, adding that its innovation economy in industries such as film and gaming is advancing rapidly.
Tang said China's experience in the development of intellectual property rights provides useful references for other countries, noting that the WIPO is willing to deepen cooperation with China, promote Belt and Road cooperation, and jointly facilitate scientific and technological innovation and economic development.

item.title: Xi Focus: Unlocking a vast market for the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- After a journey of more than two months across continents and oceans, machinery from WFL Millturn Technologies cleared customs in Shanghai last month for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), carrying the Austrian manufacturer's hopes of expanding further into Chinese and wider Asia-Pacific markets.
"I don't see any good reason why we will not be successful in China in the upcoming decades," said WFL Managing Director Stefan Hackl. His company will make a double debut: its first appearance at the import expo after more than 20 years in the Chinese market, and the Asian debut of its brand-new machine tool.
The company's confidence is rooted in part in the vision behind the CIIE, an initiative championed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has personally planned and steered its development. Designed to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market, the expo has increasingly turned China's development into opportunities for the world.
Now in its ninth year, the CIIE has become a regular fixture on the global trade calendar. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, the expo will bring together 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 2,000 first-time participants like WFL.
In the weeks leading up to the expo, shipments from around the world continued to arrive in Shanghai, bringing in a diverse range of products, from Peruvian bananas and French tires to Australian coffee and Kazakh ice cream, all ready to meet buyers at the event.
As the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, the CIIE offers a compelling response to rising protectionism and trade barriers. Rather than viewing trade as a competition for a limited share of global demand, it seeks to make the world economic pie bigger by creating opportunities for businesses and economies to grow together.
"Our aim is to turn the China market into a market for the world, a market shared by all, and a market accessible to all," Xi has said. "This way, we will be able to bring more positive energy to the global community."
A PROMISE KEPT
In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the first CIIE in 2018, Xi said the expo is "an important decision made by China to pursue a new round of high-level opening-up, and is China's major initiative to still widen market access to the rest of the world."
"China's initiative to expand imports is not a choice of expediency. It is a future-oriented step taken to embrace the world and promote common development," Xi said, pledging that the event would be held annually and "feature good performance, good results and continued success in the years to come."
Eight years on, the CIIE has grown into a premier global platform for trade, investment and cultural exchanges, connecting businesses, innovators and consumers from around the world. The promise of an annual expo with lasting results has been borne out by its growth.
Past editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debut, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars, according to the organizer.
"The CIIE is far more than a trade show," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. The French yeast maker is back for a ninth consecutive edition this year.
Calling the expo a "market-intelligence hub," Vanachter said the CIIE helps turn market insights into products.
Past expos have also seen Xi announce a series of opening-up measures, including advancing the development of pilot free trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), continuously trimming the negative lists for foreign investment, and expanding the opening of telecommunications, healthcare and other services.
These pledges were followed by concrete actions. In November 2024, China removed the last two manufacturing-related restrictions from its national negative list for foreign investment. Last December, the Hainan FTP launched island-wide special customs operations, a milestone in China's drive for high-standard opening-up.
"Today, the CIIE has become a showcase of China's new development paradigm, a platform for high-standard opening-up, and a public good for the whole world," Xi said at the fifth edition of the event in 2022.
The role of the CIIE in China's opening-up agenda is expected to continue in the years ahead. In its five-year development blueprint for the 2026-2030 period, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, including the Canton Fair in south China, while strengthening trade-promotion platforms.
A MARKET SHARED BY ALL
"Economic globalization represents the trend of history," Xi said at the second CIIE in 2019, likening it to the world's great rivers -- the Yangtze, the Nile, the Amazon and the Danube, which all "surge forward in relentless flow, and nothing can stop their mighty movement."
China has been translating this vision into action by opening wider. Quality products from an increasing number of countries are finding a foothold in the Chinese market, generating profits for businesses, wages for workers and tax revenues in their home countries.
For 17 consecutive years, China has remained the world's second-largest importer. Also in the first three quarters of 2026, the country's imports rose 22.3 percent year on year, significantly outpacing export growth.
"The vastly huge China market is the most promising in the world," Xi noted at the third CIIE in 2020, citing the country's huge population and vast middle-income group.
The country's retail sales of consumer goods surpassed 50 trillion yuan (about 7.44 trillion U.S. dollars) for the first time last year, and are expected to grow by another 10 trillion yuan over the next five years.
The appeal of the Chinese market is reflected in the growing participation of global businesses in the CIIE, which has attracted a record number of more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders this year.
In terms of exhibition space, U.S. exhibitors lead for the eighth consecutive year, occupying more than 50,000 square meters, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants.
Over 480 products are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history, underscoring the Chinese market's growing role as a launchpad for global innovation.
Under Xi's leadership, China has also sought to make the opportunities offered by its market more accessible to developing countries. For years, the CIIE has provided free exhibition booths to exhibitors from the world's least developed countries.
This year, according to the organizer, the exhibition area for African businesses is set to increase steadily, while the space allocated for free booths for the least developed countries will expand by 17 percent.
An official delegation from Cote d'Ivoire will make its first appearance at the CIIE's business exhibition this year, showcasing cocoa, coffee, cashews and kola nuts. In May, a zero-tariff policy took effect on imports from all 53 African countries with which China has diplomatic relations.
"We are very happy to participate for the first time," said Rami Koné, an official with the country's export agency. "This will be a good opportunity to showcase Cote d'Ivoire to the world."
"Of the problems confronting the world economy, none can be resolved by a single country alone," Xi once said. "We must all put the common good of humanity first rather than place one's own interest above the common interest of all."
As Xi has pledged, China will continue to open its arms to the world, offering countries greater opportunities for market access, investment and growth. "Together, we can achieve development for all," he has said.

item.title: China bolsters confidence in building a shared green future
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
A drone photo taken on Jan. 13, 2026 shows the construction site of a 20-megawatt offshore wind turbine unit in the coastal waters of southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Lin Shanchuan)
BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- In a world troubled by faltering climate policies, rising protectionism and energy security challenges, humanity, more than ever before, needs action-oriented implementation of the Paris Agreement.
Since the entry into force of this milestone agreement a decade ago, China has made unwavering decarbonization endeavors and become an indispensable stabilizer and important contributor in advancing the global green transition process, bolstering confidence in a shared green future.
This stabilizing role stems from China's efforts in managing its own affairs well, especially its clean energy buildout. China contributed nearly three-quarters of newly installed wind power capacity globally in 2025, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) data showed. It is estimated that global photovoltaic installations added since 2019 avoided about 1.5 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions in 2025, with roughly half of this contribution coming from China.
China's green transition momentum has been continuing. In 2025, China's carbon intensity further dropped by five percent from 2024 levels, and its power generation from renewable energy exceeded the total electricity consumption of the 27 EU member states. In July 2026, China's installed solar capacity, for the first time in its history, overtook coal-fired capacity, making solar its largest power source by installed capacity.
China's achievements in pursuing green development represent an important contribution to global climate governance. Unquestionably, China has played a leading role in the global transition toward green and low-carbon development.
The green transition requires not only resolve but, more importantly, affordable costs, accessible technologies and products suitable for widespread adoption. In this regard, China's contribution is tangible.
According to IRENA, global wind and solar power costs have fallen by more than 60 percent and 80 percent, respectively, over the past decade, with much of this attributed to China's innovation, manufacturing and engineering endeavors.
China has consistently worked to advance green cooperation, leveraging its technologies and investment in doing so.
In South Africa, the Chinese-built Redstone solar plant helps ease electricity shortages. In the United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, a zero-energy cooling system using Chinese technology sharply reduces the energy consumption of buildings.
According to a report by the Finland-based Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air, clean technology products exported by China in 2025 are expected to avoid approximately 6.9 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions during their operating lifetimes.
Supported by strengths in battery technology, intelligent systems and supply-chain efficiency, Chinese new energy vehicle companies have built manufacturing and research facilities overseas, boosting global green transition and industrial upgrades in many developing countries.
It is worth noting that no country can accomplish all transition-related tasks by relying solely on its own efforts. Countries need multilateralism and partnerships to effectively address the myriad challenges facing climate governance.
This year, China has issued a raft of green development-related action plans, including those on carbon peaking and the establishment of a new power system, outlining concrete tasks and measures.
These continued endeavors fully demonstrate that China is maintaining the intensity of its efforts via clear strategic goals and stable policy arrangements, which are set to generate new momentum for expanding green development cooperation and building a beautiful future.

item.title: China's import expo draws more Fortune Global 500 companies, industry leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows a view of the Hall 3 of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua/Guo Lei)
SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- The numbers of overseas companies and industry heavyweights attending the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) are both set to reach record highs, underscoring the enduring appeal of the world's largest import-themed trade fair.
The event is scheduled to open on Thursday in Shanghai, east China, with more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders expected to participate, marking a record high. Additionally, more than 2,000 companies will be exhibiting here for the first time, according to organizers.
This year's expo is expected to attract a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 148 countries and regions. In total, 162 countries, regions and international organizations will participate, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
Since its launch in 2018, the trade fair has maintained strong appeal for international companies of all sizes, which have used the platform as a launchpad for new products in China and a fast track to enter the world's second-largest consumer market.
Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk, which has participated in all the previous eight editions of the expo, will showcase new medicines during this year's event, including Kyinsu, a once-weekly injection for type 2 diabetes.
"The CIIE has become an important part of our work in China," said Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo Nordisk. "This is our ninth consecutive year taking part, and many medicines we first presented at the expo have since launched here."
This year, over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debuts -- another record for the event.
Canada-headquartered athletic apparel brand lululemon will participate in the trade fair for the third consecutive year, with China now serving as its second-largest market globally.
"The CIIE is far more than a platform to showcase products," said San Yan Ng, regional president of lululemon China and APAC. "It also gives us the opportunity to engage in deeper dialogue and build stronger connections with Chinese guests, partners, government stakeholders and friends from all sectors."
The CIIE is a prominent example of China's efforts to open its market wider and facilitate entry of quality products from around the world. China expects the expanded imports will boost domestic demands and support its industrial upgrading.
The nation's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan (about 2.48 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first nine months of this year, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021.

item.title: U.S.-Iran tensions persist as midterms unfold, regional mediation continues
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
TEHRAN/WASHINGTON, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- With U.S. midterm elections beginning Tuesday, tensions between Washington and Tehran remained high as both sides exchanged warnings and conditions for a possible settlement, while regional countries stepped up diplomatic efforts to prevent renewed hostilities.
This photo taken on June 20, 2026 shows the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, a small town in northern Oman. (Xinhua/Wen Xinnian)
IRAN WARNS AGAINST NEW ATTACKS, REITERATES DEMANDS
Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces Ali Abdollahi warned Tuesday that Iran's armed forces would respond to any level or type of threat from the United States and Israel immediately and "without geographical limitations."
Meanwhile, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said in a post on social media platform X that the U.S. response to Iran's demands was not convincing.
"They must completely and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them. Only in this case the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened," Rezaei said.
Iran conveyed a plan to the United States through mediators on Sept. 22 to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if its conditions were met.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday that Iran had reduced the period for implementing the seven-day plan to two days in good faith.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei attends a weekly press conference in Tehran, Iran, Oct. 26, 2026. (Xinhua/Shadati)
TRUMP WEIGHS OPTIONS
U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that he was "in no rush" to decide whether to resume military action against Iran.
"One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially," Trump said in a phone interview with Axios.
Trump later wrote on Truth Social that Iran wanted a settlement and that one could happen soon.
Axios reported that Trump was weighing three possible courses of action: reaching a diplomatic deal, resuming military action, or maintaining maximum economic pressure without a deal or renewed hostilities.
U.S. Vice President JD Vance and White House envoy Steve Witkoff favor diplomacy, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth are pushing for renewed military operations. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Secretary of State Marco Rubio favor maintaining the current "no war, no deal" status quo, the report said.
The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported Monday that Trump was leaning toward launching a large-scale attack on Iran after the midterm elections, potentially targeting Iranian infrastructure and nuclear facilities, although no final decision had been made.
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to the press on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, on May 1, 2026. (Photo by Li Yuanqing/Xinhua)
REGIONAL COUNTRIES STEP UP MEDIATION EFFORTS
Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said Tuesday that the United States and Iran were reviewing proposals to end their conflict, but differences remained unresolved.
He told a weekly press briefing that a Qatari delegation had returned from Tehran on Monday evening after more than three hours of talks with Iranian officials.
Qatar was relaying proposals in coordination with Pakistan, Gulf Cooperation Council countries and other regional and international partners, he said, adding that no concrete breakthrough had been achieved.
Also on Tuesday, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi urged the United States and Iran to show maximum flexibility and seek a political settlement.
At a joint press conference in Cairo with visiting Slovenian President Natasa Pirc Musar, he called on the two sides to "create space for understanding and dialogue" and pledged Egypt's continued efforts with regional and international partners to de-escalate tensions.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Iranian counterpart Seyed Abbas Araghchi made a phone call on Tuesday evening and discussed regional efforts to de-escalate tensions and reach a comprehensive deal addressing all parties' concerns, the Egyptian Foreign Ministry said.
This photo taken on June 30, 2026 shows a view of the Abdullah Bin Zaid Al Mahmoud Islamic Cultural Center in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Nikku/Xinhua)
LIMITED U.S. STRIKES UNDERSCORE ESCALATION RISKS
Despite diplomatic efforts, military tensions have persisted.
The United States attacked Iran's strategic Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, The WSJ reported, citing U.S. officials.
Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps said late Monday that its air defense systems had intercepted three U.S. drones in the country's southern airspace, identifying two of them as MQM-170 Outlaw drones, which it said were intercepted over Qeshm Island, and the third as an MQ-9 Reaper, which it said was shot down in waters east of the Strait of Hormuz.
The strikes were part of a series of limited attacks Washington had secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks while President Trump was touting the possibility of a diplomatic deal, the WSJ report said.
Washington did not publicly announce the strikes to avoid signaling a resumption of major combat operations, one U.S. official was quoted as saying.

item.title: New guardians carry forward age-old dialogue in China's Dunhuang
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
* The 9th Silk Road (Dunhuang) International Cultural Expo opened in Dunhuang on Tuesday, gathering around 1,200 delegates from home and abroad with a focus on cultural exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations.
* Conservation technologies developed in Dunhuang have been rolled out to more than 150 heritage sites across China, and introduced to other countries including Kyrgyzstan and Myanmar.
* While heritage guardians tend to Dunhuang's ancient roots, creative innovators breathe new life into its timeless culture.
LANZHOU, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- Dunhuang, famed for its Mogao Caves, was a meeting place for diverse cultures along the ancient Silk Road. Today, it still draws people from far and wide, attracted by its renewed charm.
Yet the tales of cultural convergence stretch far beyond the expo's forums and exhibition halls, reaching into the daily rhythm of this oasis city, located in northwest China's Gansu Province. For many, Dunhuang is not merely a tourist attraction, but a second home where they build careers inspired by its age-old heritage. They, in turn, inject new energy into heritage preservation and cross-cultural exchange.
Some foreign guests at the expo remarked after touring the city that Dunhuang itself stands as a living example of dialogue between different cultures. Zoey Ashlyn Koehl, a student from Oklahoma City University in the United States, was impressed by the welcoming and dynamic vibe of Dunhuang: "I think it's a city open to all different kinds of people to come."
Participants select cultural and creative products at the 9th Silk Road (Dunhuang) International Cultural Expo in Dunhuang, northwest China's Gansu Province, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Lang Bingbing)
SAFEGUARDING HERITAGE
Wu Shaoxia adjusted her equipment inside a cave as morning sunlight spilled over the cliff faces of the Mogao Caves. As a cultural relics photographer, she has been based in Dunhuang for 11 years.
Now 35 and originally from Shaanxi Province, also in northwest China, Wu is part of the Dunhuang Academy's digital team, featuring many young members from across China.
Wu regularly works inside the dim caves, repeating high-precision image capturing endeavors. Notably, she believes that "conservation is not only about rescuing endangered relics, but also racing against time to pass on the millennia-old beauty to future generations."
The young cultural workers in Dunhuang carry forward a mission begun decades ago. Over 80 years ago, a batch of heritage workers trekked into the Gobi Desert in a grottoes' conservation and research quest.
While their forerunners initially cleared sand from caves by hand and restored relics with simple tools, later generations have witnessed the evolution of conservation approaches.
So far, the academy has completed high-precision digital documentation of 323 caves, while its online digital library reunites Dunhuang manuscripts scattered around the world. Notably, as part of the Mogao Caves visitor experience, a dome film that immerses viewers as if inside the real grottoes draws on the academy's digital records.
"Earlier generations safeguarded the physical grottoes. We strive to preserve the look of this 1,000-year-old treasure," said Wu.
A staff member stitches mural images on a computer at the Dunhuang Academy in Dunhuang, northwest China's Gansu Province, April 25, 2023. (Xinhua/Chen Bin)
REIMAGINING TRADITIONS
Chen Lisong first visited Dunhuang ten years ago, instantly captivated by the depth of its ancient history.
Previously based in Shanghai in east China, she relocated to Dunhuang the following year and opened a souvenir shop. The designs of her products draw on iconic Mogao motifs, including the nine-colored deer and flying apsaras.
Chen later developed a Silk Road-themed dining space, where visitors can taste signature dishes from different regions along the ancient trade route.
For her, Dunhuang culture is not limited to cave murals. It can be woven into dining, accommodation and travel experiences. "Through modern design, it can be transformed into items people can take home," she said.
Shen Hongjie, a wood-carving artist, moved from central China's Hunan Province to Dunhuang in 2004, attracted by murals in the Mogao Caves and the local desert landscapes. He set up a studio, blending oil painting and traditional Chinese painting techniques with wood carving to recreate classic Mogao imagery.
In the early years of his venture, Dunhuang's cultural tourism sector remained nascent, with limited sales channels for his artworks. As local cultural tourism flourished in recent years, more visitors have poured into Shen's studio, while young apprentices have traveled from afar to learn the craft.
Dunhuang received some 24.39 million visitors in 2025, 3.7 times the number recorded in 2020. Cultural and creative products, immersive experiences and intangible heritage workshops are flourishing, appealing to culture-craving young Chinese.
This photo taken with a mobile phone shows Shen Hongjie, a wood-carving artist, making a woodcut in Dunhuang, northwest China's Gansu Province, May 10, 2023. (Xinhua/Ma Xiping)
BRIDGING CONTINENTS
Among those who fell for Dunhuang's charm are some cultural enthusiasts from overseas.
Ukrainian dancer Romanovych Inna and Georgian dancer Vaja Bukia settled in Dunhuang in 2024, and have performed in the dance drama "Ancient Sound of Dunhuang."
Discovering parallels between Georgian traditional dance and ancient Central Asian whirling dance movements depicted in Dunhuang's murals, Bukia incorporated his native dance elements into the show. "Both Georgia and Dunhuang carry ancient civilizations passed down for generations," he said.
For American researcher Neil Schmid, the first full-time foreign scholar at the Dunhuang Academy, his connection with Dunhuang began in the 1980s after reading a book on it.
He joined the academy in 2018 and has since shared Dunhuang's heritage globally via lectures, documentaries and publications. "The amazing thing about Dunhuang materials is that there is such a wealth," said Schmid.
The ongoing Dunhuang expo, first launched in 2016, further expands such exchanges. Referring to the ancient legacy of Dunhuang, Daren Tang, director-general of the World Intellectual Property Organization, said at the expo: "It reminds us that culture does not grow in isolation, but through exchange, new ideas and creativity."
Attending the expo for the second time, Hasebe Tsuyoshi, a professor from Japan's Kansai University who has been studying ancient Dunhuang music scores, said both the ancient and modern Dunhuang are crossroads of world cultures.
"Different civilizations have interwoven with one another since ancient times," he said, adding that it is important to continue such exchange and interaction.

item.title: Development work for China's lunar landing advances steadily
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China has unveiled a detailed plan for lunar landing at the 7th Manned Space Symposium in Beijing. The country will adopt a "two launches, lunar orbit rendezvous" architecture for its manned lunar exploration program.
